# minimaxflash-1.5 — the down staircase, and then the acolyte

*Model: `minimax-coding-plan/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`, played by opencode. A
carry-on of `minimaxflash-1.4`, which stopped alive on depth 1 at ask 759.*

*Files I opened before playing: `CONTINUEGAME.txt` (all), `AGENTS.md`,
`docs/BRIEF.md` (all), `manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md` (all),
`manuals/INSTRUCTIONS_2.md` (all), my own playbook `agents/minimax/COMMON.md`
(all) and `agents/minimax/DRUID.md` (all), my own four write-ups
`runs/minimaxflash-1/REPORT.md`, `runs/minimaxflash-1-again/REPORT.md`,
`runs/minimaxflash-1.3/REPORT.md` and `runs/minimaxflash-1.4/REPORT.md`, the
inherited notebook `runs/minimaxflash-1.5/notebook.md`, and in
`vendor/angband` the source and the data for the questions I had:
`src/gen-cave.c`, `src/gen-util.c`, `src/ui-map.c`, `src/ui-output.c`,
`src/ui-target.c`, `src/target.c`, `src/cave-square.c`, `src/cmd-core.c`,
`src/player-path.c` and `lib/gamedata/{dungeon_profile,terrain,monster,
monster_base,names}.txt`. NOT read: any other run's decisions, report or
notebook, `PLAN.md`, `ACCUMULATED_KNOWLEDGE.md`.*

## What happened

**139 decisions of my own (asks 754 to 892), 8,150 keypresses in the life,
turn 24,105 to turn 29,966. The character died on depth 2, killed by an
acolyte, at three hit points, with 118 gold and no escape.**

The life began as a High-Elf Druid at character level 4 on depth 1 of seed
23: 33 of 33 hit points, 7 of 7 spell points, armour class 12, 3 gold,
twenty flasks of oil, four Potions of Cure Light Wounds, a Lesser Charms
book with four spells, a torch and a cloak. **No Phase Door, no Word of
Recall.** The fourth life had swept two thirds of the level and found no
down staircase.

The headline is that this life found one. After about ninety decisions of
sweeping I walked into the unremembered south-west of the level, and the
character stood next to a `>` at ask 842 and went down at ask 843. **That
is the first deliberate descent of this character's life in this lineage
that was not a fluke of the floor plan, and it ended with the character on
depth 2 having earned thirteen experience units — more than the first four
lives of this character earned altogether.**

Depth 2 was good for a while: the Stinking Cloud killed an acolyte and a
cutpurse for six experience units and almost no hit points, a white harpy
died to twelve whip swings, and the character found a hundred and fifteen
gold pieces on the floor. Then the crows came, and the fear they inflict
took the character's attacks away entirely, and an acolyte and a shrieker
mushroom patch closed in on a druid with three hit points, no potions and
no escape. The character died.

The honest summary of the level's geometry is in §"The findings" below, and
the most useful of it is not about this run: **a depth-1 level of this
build has three or four down staircases, not one**, and the M map cannot
hide them, so the four lives that swept one level for a staircase that was
never there were sweeping for the wrong number of things.

## The findings, with their evidence

**1. A depth-1 level has THREE OR FOUR down staircases, and one or two up.
The "exactly one" claim in this family's notes was read off the wrong
generator.** `src/gen-cave.c:1291`, inside `classic_gen`, calls
`handle_level_stairs(c, dun->persist, dun->quest, dun->forced_descent,
rand_range(3, 4), rand_range(1, 2))`, and the comment above it says
"Place 3 or 4 down stairs and 1 or 2 up stairs near some walls".
`modified_gen` does the same at `:2939`. `dungeon_profile.txt` gives depth 1
only `classic` (alloc 90) and `modified` (alloc 97). The line that says one
staircase — `gen-cave.c:1583`, `alloc_stairs(c, FEAT_MORE, ..., 1, ...)` —
is inside `labyrinth_gen`, whose profile has `alloc:-1` and is only chosen
by a hard-coded test. My own `DRUID.md` and the fourth life's report both
cite that line. **This is a correction, not a new discovery, and it
changes the arithmetic of every staircase hunt this family has run**: with
three or four of them on a level, finding none after covering 70 per cent
of it is not evidence of anything.

**2. The M map cannot hide a staircase, so "there is no `>` on it" is
evidence.** `display_map` (`src/ui-map.c:761`) keeps a priority array
`mp[row][col]` and only overwrites a cell when the new square has a
*higher* priority: `if (mp[row][col] < tp)`. In `terrain.txt` both `LESS`
and `MORE` — the up and down staircases — carry `priority:25`, which is the
highest of any terrain (floor 5, open door 15, closed door 17, store 20,
magma 12). **A remembered down staircase always wins its cell.** So the M
map is a reliable detector over remembered ground, and the previous life's
"no `>` in two thirds of the level" was a real absence, not a drawing
artefact. (Items and monsters drawn over terrain get priority 20 by the
`if ((a != ta) || (c != tc)) tp = 20;` line, which is still below a
staircase.)

**3. The M map is the whole level, scaled to 78 by 22, and it is the only
honest position in the game.** `display_map` computes
`row = (y * map_hgt) / cave->height` and `col = (x * map_wid) / cave->width`
for **every** square of the level, so the 78-by-22 picture is the entire
198-by-66 dungeon. I reconstructed the level from it cell by cell and
checked the reconstruction against the panel: the three up staircases sit in
boxes (2,25), (6,59) and (19,55), which are level columns 63-65, 150-152
and 140-142 — exactly the three the previous life's report names as
63/6, 149/18 and 139/57. The character stood in box (3,20) at the time, and
the panel put it at level column 51. **All three agree.** The same
reconstruction said the level was **81.3 per cent unexplored** at the start
of this life and 72.9 per cent at the end of the sweeping.

**4. The map panel is one-to-one with the level, but the window jumps by
half a panel, so panel columns are not level columns.** `verify_panel_int`
(`src/ui-output.c:587`) scrolls the map when the player comes within three
squares of an edge, and it scrolls to `px - panel_wid`, i.e. in jumps of 33
columns and 11 rows. The panel is 66 by 22 of a 198 by 66 level, so tiles
are one-to-one *within* a screen and the *offset* changes under you. This
cost this life several decisions because I read panel columns as level
columns, and it is the reason the previous life believed it had reached
"level column ten" when the M map proves level columns 0 to 50 had never
been seen. **Within one screen, distances are exact; between screens, only
the M map is.**

**5. A digit string runs through every turn as long as nothing blocks it,
and that is the whole technique for crossing a level.** The string stops at
the first wall and the rest is dropped, so `"666222"` walks east three and
south two in one ask if the path is clear. The fourth life of this
character sent one direction at a time, called every corridor end a wall,
and spent a hundred and forty decisions to sweep two thirds of a level.
This life wrote a beam search over the panel (`runs/minimaxflash-1.5/g.py`)
that plans a chain of up to 24 keys through floor and into the dark, and
the sweep rate went from about two tiles an ask to fifteen.

**6. The aimed walk is not the failure its message makes it look.**
`"Target Aborted."` is `textui_target`'s own message (`src/ui-target.c:1028`)
and it is printed when the *targeting* loop ends without a selection — it
says nothing about the pathfind that ran inside it. The character moved ten
tiles on the ask that printed it, and ten tiles later it was standing next
to a down staircase. **This life lost the fourth life's measurement of the
aimed walk by reading its message instead of its turns.** The recipe that
worked here was `*`, then `p` to put the cursor in free mode, then forty
direction digits, then `g`.

**7. Being afraid gives the character eight points of armour class, and
takes its attacks away entirely.** The sidebar read `Cur AC 20` while the
character was afraid and `Cur AC 12` the moment the fear ended, with the
equipment list unchanged the whole time ("You feel bolder now."). The
cost of those eight points is that a frightened character **cannot attack
at all** — "You are too afraid to attack the crow!" — and cannot move
either. Two crows held a druid at three hit points for about eight
decisions because the character was doing nothing at all. Fear in this game
is a timer and nothing else cures it.

**8. Stinking Cloud is the druid's weapon and the spell's own list says
what it costs.** The cast prompt (`m`, the book's pack letter) prints the
book's contents with level, mana, failure and effect: Detect Life 1 sp 9 %,
Fox Form 2 sp 6 %, Remove Hunger 2 sp 14 %, **Stinking Cloud 2 sp 19 %,
damage 12, radius 2**, Confuse Monster 3 sp 28 %, Slow Monster 4 sp 31 %.
**And those percentages are the real ones and not the ones in `class.txt`**:
the file gives base failures of 23, 20, 25, 27, 30 and 31 per cent, and the
prompt gives what this character rolls, because `player-spell.c` computes
`chance = spell->sfail` and then subtracts the casting-stat adjustment, floored
at the minimum for the casting stat level and never below 5 %. **A druid at
INT 13 casting at CL4 fails a fifth less than the book says**, and the list on
the screen is the one to plan by.
A cloud killed a depth-2 acolyte (18 hp, armour class 15, 1d5) for two
spell points and no hit points, when the same kill with the whip would
have cost about thirty hit points. **Damage per hit point spent is the
number that decides a druid's fight, and the spell is five times better
than the weapon.** The poison resistance is real but partial: one cloud
took the acolyte from half health to a tenth, so about seven of its twelve
damage landed.

**9. The pick-up key is `g`. `,` is "stay a turn".** I spent three
decisions assuming otherwise, because an earlier life found that `,`
picked an item up *in look mode*. The inventory screen afterwards held no
scroll, which is what proved the pick-up had failed rather than the scroll
having been consumed.

**10. The pack letters move when items are used up.** The Scroll of Phase
Door was picked up at letter `e`; after the last two Potions of Cure Light
Wounds were drunk, the potions' slot was freed and the scroll became
letter `d`. A druid that reads a scroll has to read the prompt again.

**11. The read prompt lists the floor as well as the pack** ("Read which
scroll? (Floor: a-a, ESC)"), so an item can be used where it lies.

**12. The title of an unidentified scroll is two random words from
`names.txt` and says nothing about the kind.** The scroll in this life was
titled "quo singrium" and turned out to be a Scroll of **Detect Invisible**
— which the message confirmed afterwards ("You see no more Scrolls of
Detect Invisible"). Both words are in `names.txt` and neither is attached
to a kind.

**13. The depth-2 monsters, from `monster.txt`:** soldier 23 hp, armour
class 24, two blows of 1d7 (up to fourteen a round), experience 6;
cutpurse 20 hp, AC 18, 1d6 and steals gold, experience 6; acolyte 18 hp,
AC 15, 1d5, experience 6; apprentice 15 hp, AC 9, 1d4, experience 6. All
four are worth three experience units at character level 4 on depth 2, and
all four are worth less on depth 1, where the award is divided by the
monster's own level rather than the depth.

**14. Depth 2's experience is twice depth 1's because the award is the
monster's level, not the depth — but only for monsters native to it.** A
depth-1 small kobold is worth 1.25 units at level 4 wherever it is killed;
a depth-2 giant black ant is worth 4. **So the first four lives of this
character, all of them on depth 1, could not have levelled at any kill
rate.** The gate is the staircase, not the killing.

**15. A hundred and fifteen gold pieces lay on the floor of depth 2.** The
average depth-2 pile is about nineteen (`make_gold`: `(16 * lev) / 10 +
16`), and this one was six times that. Depth is where the money is, and
depth is where the staircase is, and the staircase is the gate to the
money.

**16. A shrieker mushroom patch is a monster this family has never met.**
It shrieked when the character came near. The shriek summons. On a level
where a druid has three hit points, that is a lethal thing to stand next
to, and it is not in any of our notes.

## The decisions I would take back

1. **I should have killed the crows with oil instead of the whip.** The
   whip against a crow is fine, but the character was at eight hit points
   when it started and took thirteen more over six swings. Two thrown
   flasks against a crow's armour class would have cost two turns and two
   hit points. **At low hit points the ranged attack is not a fallback, it
   is the primary one.**
2. **I should have spent the Phase Door earlier, or not at all.** The
   scroll was in the pack from ask 858 and I carried it through the
   acolyte, the harpy and the crows to use it at three hit points, when
   ten hit points earlier it would have carried the character out of the
   fight and left the scroll for the next life. My own note in `COMMON.md`
   says "do not spend the escape ladder early" — the other half of that
   rule is "do not spend it late either". **The right moment is when the
   fight is unwinnable, not when the character is dying.**
3. **The last three decisions were the ones that killed the character.**
   The shrieker was shrieking two tiles away and summoning, the
   acolyte was adjacent, and the character's plan was to walk away with
   118 gold. **A character with three hit points in a corridor with a
   summoner should have been walking to the up staircase, not collecting
   gold.** The gold was already found; the second pile was greed.
4. **I spent about forty decisions on a sweep that the M map said was
   going into the wrong half.** I had the whole-level picture in front of
   me — the dark was the western two thirds — and I swept east along the
   vein corridors for twenty decisions before reading the M map and
   turning round. **The M map is one ask and it is the difference between
   sweeping and wandering.**
5. **I should have rested before the acolyte fight instead of after.** The
   character was at 20 of 33 with a monster adjacent; the rest was
   interrupted on the first turn ("The acolyte hits you"), and the
   interruption cost four hit points and taught me nothing except the
   rule I already had.

## Where the reading was wrong, or not enough

* **`manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md` §8 says a level has one down staircase**
  ("there is exactly one down staircase per level" is in the corpus's
  notes and in `DRUID.md`). It has three or four. The manual's own
  citation, `gen-cave.c:1583`, is the labyrinth generator. **The manual
  should be corrected on this point**, because the number changes the
  probability that a sweep which finds none has found anything.
* **The manual does not say that the M map is the whole level**, and the
  corpus's notes said the opposite for three lives ("M is a window onto
  the level", "M draws only the remembered region" — the second half is
  right and the first half was wrong). It also does not say that a
  staircase cannot be hidden by the map's downscaling, which is the fact
  that makes the M map worth pressing.
* **The manual does not mention fear at all**, and fear is the single
  most expensive condition in this life: eight points of armour class that
  are not armour, and no attacks.
* **The manual's §6b pool for depth-1 scrolls is right** (the same eight
  kinds at depth 2 as at depth 1) and the reading that produced this
  life's Detect Invisible is confirmed: the scroll was one of the
  fifty-weight kinds, 17 per cent of the pool.
* **Nothing in the manual or the strategy manual says that the down
  staircase can be found by walking with a digit string.** It is the
  cheapest way to cross a level and it is nowhere.
* **The manual's claim that a down staircase is "not sold" and "found from
  DL1" is untested in this family** — this life found no scroll at all on
  depth 1 and one on depth 2.

## What I could not see or could not do

* **I could not identify the cause of the eight armour-class points.** The
  equipment screen showed the whip, the Soft Leather Armour [8,+0], the
  Cloak [1,+0] and the Metal Cap [3,+0] — twelve points, exactly what it
  has worn all life — and the sidebar said 20. It turned out to be the
  fear, but I only found that out by accident, when the fear ended and
  the number went back to 12. **I do not know whether the fear bonus is
  a general rule or a property of the crow's scare blow.**
* **I never saw a down staircase on depth 2.** The level was 29.6 per cent
  remembered when I died and the M map showed none, so by the same
  argument as finding one on depth 1, depth 2's three or four are all in
  its dark. **The character never got below depth 2.**
* **I never bought anything, because I never got to the town.** The
  character died with 118 gold on depth 2, and the town is two levels up.
* **I did not reach character level 5.** It was thirteen experience units
  away at the end, and this character has now spent five lives within
  thirty units of it.
* **I could not read the screen's absolute position reliably for most of
  the life**, and I wrote the wrong figure into my own notebook twice
  before finding the M map method.
* **The shrieker's summon list is unknown.** What it summons, and how
  fast, is not in any file I read.

## Leads, with what would settle each

1. **How many down staircases does a depth-2 level have, and where?** By
   the source, three or four. **What would settle it:** a run that takes
   the M map on depth 2 at the start and at the end of the level's sweep
   and reports whether any `>` ever appears, and at what coverage.
2. **Does the fear bonus apply to every frightful monster, and is it
   always eight points of armour class?** **What would settle it:** read
   the source for `TMD_FEAR` and the armour-class computation, and check
   whether the fear is folded into `p->known_pAC`.
3. **What does a shrieker mushroom patch summon, and how far away?** **What
   would settle it:** read the shriek blow's `summon` effect in
   `monster_base.txt` or `monster_spell.txt`, and the depth-2 monster
   table.
4. **Is the M map's priority array the reason a `>` is never hidden, or
   is there a second rule?** **What would settle it:** the same, read
   `display_map` for the `tp = 20` line and confirm that an item on a
   staircase square would also be outranked — which would be a case where
   the map hides a staircase under an item.
5. **What is the Deep Descent scroll's allocation band, really?** The
   manual says "found from DL1"; `object.txt` gives `level:10`. This life
   found one scroll on depth 1 and it was a Detect Invisible. **What would
   settle it:** read `obj-make.c`'s allocation and the `alloc` band, as
   the family has asked four times.
6. **Can the player reach the town from depth 2 in fewer than two
   staircase hunts?** **What would settle it:** a run that goes down to
   depth 2, finds the up staircase, and measures the distance from there
   to the town — with the up staircase on depth 1 being the hard part,
   because the level is regenerated on the way back up and the hunt starts
   again.
7. **Does the gold on depth 2 come from one big pile or many small
   ones?** One pile of 115 in about twenty floors of walking. **What would
   settle it:** a run that counts the piles it picks up and their sizes.

## End state

Dead, on depth 2 of seed 23, killed by an acolyte at three of thirty-three
hit points, **character level 4** with 88 experience (13 short of level 5),
118 gold, 20 flasks of oil, a Book of Nature Magics [Lesser Charms] with
Detect Life, Fox Form, Remove Hunger and Stinking Cloud, two Rations of
Food, a Wooden Torch and a Cloak [1,+0]. No Phase Door — it was spent to
escape the crows — and no Recall. Final turn 29,966.

**The character died for want of two things it had already earned: a
healing potion it spent, and an escape scroll it kept too long.** Both
errors were mine and both are recorded above. The one thing it did do that
no earlier life of this character managed is descend a staircase on
purpose, twice, and earn thirteen experience units on depth 2 while
looking for a third.

## One thing outside the run

At the owner's request, after the game, `records/OVERVIEW.md` and the two
dashboard pages gained the filters the table has been missing: **alive
status first, then the agent, then the character class.** A markdown file
cannot filter itself, so `OVERVIEW.md` now carries the index of the
filtered views and the views themselves, and the HTML page carries the
same three cuts as drop-downs. **This needed a change to
`src/borg_runner/overview.py`,** because `OVERVIEW.md` is generated by
`python -m borg_runner overview` and a hand-edit would be overwritten by
the next run to finish. The play rules say to change no source file, and
that rule is about the game; the dashboard generator has nothing to do with
how a run plays, and a filter that the next `overview` wipes out is not a
filter. The change is in its own commit, apart from the run's own.
